transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, good day to you, sir! What brings you down to these parts? The forge is a bit quieter than usual, as you might notice. The master smiths, including Brokkr himself, have ventured deep into the Great Veins. Searching for that rare, shimmering ore, you understand. Won't be back for weeks, I reckon. But... well, you're welcome to warm yourself by the coals, if you like. They still hold some heat.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Ah, Brokkr's absence seems quite unfortunate. However, I am here on more pressing matters. I have recently discovered that the new war-hammer I had commission from you dwarves lacks the proper balance and has misspelled runes on its surface. I am here to demand that it be reforged immediately."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, a new war-hammer, you say? Misspelled runes and off-balance? That... that's certainly not the usual standard of Brokkr's workshop, I assure you. Most unusual indeed.

However, as I mentioned, the masters are deep in the mines. And I mean *deep*. Beyond the reach of even the keenest ear or the loudest shout, chasing after some mythical star-iron. They won't be returning for many weeks, perhaps even months, until their quest is fulfilled.

And regarding reforging, sir... well, the standing policy of Brokkr's workshop, and indeed, all commissions from the Sons of Ivaldi, is quite clear. All commissions are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. Even a god must wait until the next forging-season, and, if it's an entirely new request, pay anew. I'm just the apprentice, you understand, but those are the rules set down by the masters themselves. My hands are tied on that front, I'm afraid.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Brokkr's rules and policies be they. Yet, I cannot simply accept this inferior craftsmanship. The war-hammer must be reforged without delay. It is a matter of utmost importance and necessity. I will not wait for weeks or months, much less the next forging season. I demand your attention and action on this matter immediately."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I... I understand your frustration, sir. Truly, I do. Inferior craftsmanship is a grave insult to any smith. But... but I am merely the apprentice. I've only just begun to learn the ways of the forge, to understand the intricacies of shaping metal and inscribing runes with true power. To reforge a war-hammer for... well, for someone of your evident stature, that's a task for a master, not for a fledgling like myself.

And the masters *are* unreachable. Their oath to find the star-iron takes them far beyond the common tunnels, to places where even the echoes of this world fade. They won't return until their purpose is met. And the policy... it's not *my* policy, it's *the* policy. Set down by Brokkr himself, and Sindri, and the great smiths before them. To defy it... I couldn't, even if I possessed the skill, which I most certainly do not. I would be banished, at best! My apologies, sir, but my hands are truly bound.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Your apologies are noted, but I will not be swayed by such excuses. The safety and needs of Asgard must come first. I cannot allow this inferior war-hammer to remain in circulation. I will speak to the other gods and seek their assistance in rectifying this situation. We shall not wait for the next forging season."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I... I see. You mean to bring this to the attention of the other Aesir. I understand the gravity of the situation, especially if it concerns the safety of Asgard. That's... that's a serious matter indeed.

However, I must again stress, sir, that my position here is merely as an apprentice. I hold no authority to overturn the established policies of Brokkr's workshop, nor do I possess the immense skill required to even attempt such a reforge myself. The master smiths are truly, truly deep in the earth, far beyond any message, pursuing an ancient quest. Their return is not within my power to hasten.

And the policy, about fulfilled commissions and the new forging season... that is the way it has always been, decreed by the masters. It is not something I, a humble apprentice, could ever hope to change, even under du… even if I were ordered to. My apologies, again, but I am utterly powerless to assist with your request directly.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Your apologies are accepted. I appreciate your honesty, despite your limitations as an apprentice. I understand that the situation is complex and that there are constraints to your actions. But I implore you to consider the urgency of this matter. The safety of Asgard must not be compromised. If the other gods and I cannot bring about a solution, then we will take matters into our own hands. We will find a way to ensure that this inferior war-hammer does not enter the hands of those who can use it to harm our realm."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I... I hear you, sir, and I understand the weight of your words regarding Asgard's safety. It's a concern that resonates even in these deep halls. A compromised weapon, especially one from our forge, is a serious matter.

But as I've said, the masters... they are truly beyond reach. They've sealed themselves off to focus entirely on their quest for the star-iron. No message, no plea, however urgent, could possibly get through to them until they decide their task is done. And for me, to even attempt to touch a weapon of such power, let alone reforge it... I simply don't have the skill or the authority. It would be a disaster, I assure you.

I wish there was something, anything, I could do. But the rules are set, the masters are gone, and I am but a novice. My most sincere apologies that I cannot offer more than the warmth of these dying coals.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you for your understanding, Brokkr's apprentice. Your sincere apologies are appreciated. While I am disappointed by the current circumstances, I appreciate your honesty and dedication to maintaining the integrity of the forge's policies. Rest assured, we will find a solution to this predicament. Whether it be through the intervention of the other gods or through other means, we will ensure that the safety of Asgard is not compromised. Until then, I thank you for your service."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Thank you, sir. I... I truly hope a solution can be found, for Asgard's sake. It weighs on me, the thought of a faulty weapon. I'll continue to tend the fires and hone my own skills, awaiting the masters' return. May your quest for a resolution be swift and successful. Safe travels back to Asgard.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Brokkr's apprentice. Your dedication to the forge is commendable. Rest assured, we will find a way to rectify this situation. Your continued service is valued, and we appreciate your efforts. Now, let us proceed to the forge and make sure that the new war-hammer meets the standards we expect from a weapon crafted by the Sons of Ivaldi."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Sir, I... I am very grateful for your kind words about my dedication, truly. But when I suggested "proceeding to the forge," I meant for *my* duties, for tending the coals and practicing the simpler forms of metalwork. To actually... "make sure the new war-hammer meets the standards" by taking it to the forge for *reforging*... that, I simply cannot do.

As I've tried to explain, sir, I am but a fledgling apprentice. I lack the profound skill, the experience, and certainly the authority to even touch, let alone re-craft, a weapon of such power and importance. And the master smiths, who *do* possess that skill, they are deep, deep in the earth, on a quest that will keep them away for weeks, perhaps months. They are truly unreachable.

The policy, too, stands firm: commissions are fulfilled upon delivery. I am bound by these rules, and by my own limited abilities. My apologies, again, but I cannot assist in that way. I am here only to keep the workshop ready for the masters' return, not to undertake their tasks.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Your apologies are noted once more, Brokkr's apprentice. I understand your limitations as an apprentice, and I respect the boundaries of your duties within the forge. However, the safety and effectiveness of Asgard's defenses are at stake. We cannot simply rely on the return of the master smiths to resolve this issue. We must find another way to ensure that the war-hammer meets the standards we expect from a weapon crafted by the Sons of Ivaldi."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
I truly wish I could, sir, I do. The thought of a weapon crafted here being anything less than perfect... it troubles me deeply. But "another way" that involves this forge, right now, with only myself present, for *that* hammer... it simply isn't possible.

My role, while the masters are away, is to keep the fires banked, the tools polished, and the workshop ready for their return. To maintain what *is* here, not to create or correct what *they* have already delivered. I am sworn to that, and limited by my unproven hands.

I understand the urgency you feel for Asgard, and I respect your determination to find a solution. But my part in that, I'm afraid, cannot extend to touching the hammer itself. That would require the master's touch, and they are beyond reach. Perhaps... perhaps the "other way" you speak of lies outside of Brokkr's immediate workshop, until they return.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Your understanding of your duties as an apprentice is commendable. Your adherence to the established roles and responsibilities within the forge is crucial. I appreciate your loyalty to maintaining the readiness of the workshop while the master smiths are away. However, the safety of Asgard requires us to find a solution, even if it means seeking help from beyond the confines of Brokkr's workshop."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Yes, sir, I concur. It seems that for this particular challenge, the solution will indeed have to be found beyond these walls, at least until the masters return from their deep delving. My oath is to this workshop and its readiness for *their* craft, not to perform it myself.

I wish you good fortune in your search, and for the safety of Asgard. May the other gods be swift in their aid.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Brokkr's apprentice, for your understanding and cooperation. Your loyalty to the forge is commendable. Now, let us proceed with our visit to the other gods and seek their guidance on this matter."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Very well, sir. May your journey be fruitful, and your discussions with the other gods bring about the resolution you seek. I will continue to guard the forge as best I can until the masters return. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Farewell, Brokkr's apprentice. I trust you will continue to serve the forge diligently in the meantime. We shall meet again, when the moment is right."
